classification.difficultyReason: The equal-root representation and sum/product choices are supplied; the student links those relations to the parameter, tangent equation and contact point.

content.prompt:
Consider the line $y=2x+k$ and the parabola $y=x^2-4x$.

(a) Show that the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection satisfy the equation
$$x^2-6x-k=0.$$

(b) Suppose that the line is a tangent to the parabola; in other words, the two roots of the quadratic equation are equal. Let the roots be $\alpha$ and $\alpha$.

(i) Using sum of roots, show that $\alpha=3$.

(ii) Using product of roots, show that $\alpha^2=-k$ and hence find $k$.

(iii) Therefore, state the equation of the tangent line and find its point of contact with the parabola.

answer.short: $x^2-6x-k=0$; $\alpha=3$; $\alpha^2=-k$, so $k=-9$. Tangent line: $y=2x-9$. Point of contact: $(3,-3)$.
answer.worked:
(a)
$$\begin{aligned}2x+k&=x^2-4x\\x^2-6x-k&=0\end{aligned}$$
(b)(i)
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\alpha&=-\frac{b}{a}\\2\alpha&=-\frac{-6}{1}\\2\alpha&=6\\\alpha&=3\end{aligned}$$
(ii)
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha\times\alpha&=\frac{c}{a}\\\alpha^2&=-k\\3^2&=-k\\k&=-9\end{aligned}$$
(iii) The tangent line is $y=2x-9$.
At the point of contact, PSF: Product $9$, Sum $-6$, Factors $-3$ and $-3$.
$$\begin{aligned}x^2-6x+9&=0\\(x-3)^2&=0\\x&=3\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}y&=2(3)-9\\&=-3\end{aligned}$$
The point of contact is $(3,-3)$.
